title: Ada and the Signal
premise: Juniper Fairweather, a xenolinguist whose mind has been so reshaped by alien languages that he no longer dreams in human tongues, works the long haul routes between colonies that have gone silent since the war began. When a distress signal arrives in Vessic — a language extinct for two hundred years, one only Juniper can half-read — he is conscripted by both sides of the war, each convinced the message will legitimize their claim to the dead colony world of Ada. As he deciphers it, Juniper discovers the signal is not distress but testimony: the Vessic were exterminated by the very government now claiming their world, and the message is a warning meant for whoever comes next. In the end, Juniper must choose between delivering the truth and preserving the fragile ceasefire — and he chooses truth, broadcasting the message in every language he knows, human and otherwise, at the cost of his career, his citizenship, and the last shreds of the man he used to be.
about_author: Ines Nystrom is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent eleven years relaying messages between ships that rarely answered. They write about language, distance, and the people who carry words across the dark.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Juniper pilots the relay ship Meridian through the silent corridor between colonies, logging dead frequencies. POV: Juniper. Establishes his fractured inner life — he dreams in a language no living person speaks. Emotional beat: loneliness worn smooth into routine.

chapters.title: A Grammar of Silence
chapters.summary: At Waystation Kettle, Juniper visits the linguistics archive and argues with archivist Sefa Oyelaran about whether extinct languages can truly be reconstructed or only mourned. POV: Juniper. He admits he can no longer read his own childhood letters without translation. Beat: quiet grief disguised as academic debate.

chapters.title: Signal in an Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: The Meridian intercepts a repeating transmission from the Ada system — structured, urgent, unmistakably Vessic, a language extinct two centuries. POV: Juniper. His hands shake as he recognizes phonemes he's only seen in burial inscriptions. Beat: awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Conscription
chapters.summary: Juniper reports the signal per protocol; within hours, Republic intelligence officer Captain Idris Vane arrives and seizes both ship and linguist. POV: Juniper. Vane is courteous, absolute, and makes clear refusal means detention. Beat: the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: What the Republic Wants
chapters.summary: Aboard the warship Resolute, Juniper learns the Republic claims Ada by inheritance and believes the signal supports its claim. He begins formal decryption under supervision. POV: Juniper, with glimpses of Vane's private doubts. Beat: complicity beginning, rationalized.

chapters.title: The Coalition Listens
chapters.summary: Coalition forces intercept the Resolute's convoy but, instead of attacking, demand Juniper be handed over — they too have decoded fragments. A tense parley ends in joint custody. POV: alternating Juniper and Coalition analyst Mirei Sol. Beat: the war briefly pausing around one man.

chapters.title: Two Keys
chapters.summary: Juniper works with Mirei, whose grandmother spoke a creole descended from Vessic trade-pidgin. Their methods clash — his intuition, her rigor — but the first full sentence emerges: 'We who remain.' POV: Mirei primarily. Beat: reluctant partnership, first warmth.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Vessic
chapters.summary: Immersion in the signal deepens; Juniper begins dreaming fully in Vessic and loses chunks of English mid-conversation. Mirei notices him answering questions before they're asked. POV: Juniper. Beat: transformation accelerating, wonder mixed with self-erosion.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how Juniper acquired his gift — an experimental immersion program after the frontier massacres, trading his native linguistic instincts for fluency in dying tongues. POV: Juniper past and present interwoven. Beat: understanding what he already paid, and what's being asked again.

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Captain Vane privately offers Juniper amnesty and reinstatement if he certifies the message as a Republic loyalist testament. Juniper realizes Vane suspects the truth too. POV: Vane. Beat: temptation offered by a man who hates offering it.

chapters.title: Breakthrough
chapters.summary: Mirei's creole key unlocks the grammatical structure; the message resolves into a narrative, not a plea. It is dated before the Vessic extinction event. POV: Mirei. The word 'witness' appears forty times. Beat: dread dawning — this is not distress, it's evidence.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Full decryption: the Vessic recorded their own extermination by the Republic's founding generation, and hid the record in a beacon timed to activate when their world was claimed again. The message names Ada as a grave, not a prize. POV: Juniper. Beat: devastation; the war's foundation is a lie.

chapters.title: Quarantine of Truth
chapters.summary: Both governments move to classify the translation. Vane orders Juniper confined; the Coalition recalls Mirei. The two are separated mid-argument about what to do. POV: alternating. Beat: institutions closing ranks, allies torn apart.

chapters.title: The Ceasefire Clock
chapters.summary: Armistice talks at Ada approach; whichever side holds the planet when the treaty signs owns it. Both fleets converge. Juniper, in detention, realizes the message must be public before signing or the lie becomes law forever. POV: Juniper. Beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: Sefa's Archive
chapters.summary: Juniper escapes with help from an unexpected ally: Vane, who cannot stomach certifying a lie, smuggles him toward a transmitter — but demands Juniper accept the consequences alone. POV: Vane. Beat: redemption purchased at another's cost.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: From the Meridian's ancient array, Juniper transmits the full testimony in Vessic, then translates it live into eleven languages, his voice fraying as his English deteriorates mid-broadcast. POV: Juniper. Beat: climax — truth spoken at the cost of self.

chapters.title: Fleets Holding Breath
chapters.summary: Both armadas receive the broadcast. Soldiers on both sides share Vessic ancestry; mutiny ripples through squadrons. Commanders order advance anyway. POV: Mirei aboard a Coalition ship watching crews refuse. Beat: the war cracking from within.

chapters.title: Ada Orbit
chapters.summary: Juniper flies the unarmed Meridian between the fleets, broadcasting on all bands, daring them to fire on the messenger. A single shot cripples the ship; both sides freeze. POV: Juniper, wounded, still transmitting. Beat: sacrifice made literal.

chapters.title: The Landing
chapters.summary: Ceasefire declared in chaos. Ground teams land on Ada and find the Vessic vault — physical proof matching the signal. Mirei leads the verification. POV: Mirei. Beat: grief and vindication entangled; a graveyard finally acknowledged.

chapters.title: Treaty of Witnesses
chapters.summary: The armistice is rewritten: Ada becomes neutral memorial ground governed jointly, its history taught in both academies. Juniper, recovering, is offered honors by both sides and refuses them all. POV: Juniper. Beat: belonging found outside nations.

chapters.title: What He Dreams Now
chapters.summary: Months later, Juniper teaches Vessic to children of both worlds, including Mirei's young relatives. His English returns slowly, imperfectly; his dreams now hold both tongues. POV: Juniper. Beat: healing as integration, not restoration.

chapters.title: The Signal Continues
chapters.summary: Final chapter: a new faint signal arrives from deeper space — older than Vessic, stranger. Juniper smiles, packs his grammar books, and signs onto the long route again, no longer running from silence but toward voices. POV: Juniper. Beat: hopeful open ending; the work continues.
